You are synthesizing a unified hypothesis from multiple parent hypotheses.
Goal: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.

TITLE: DINO-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
SUMMARY: Train with image-level MIL first, then refine the resulting patch maps of abnormal source images by random-walk propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph into pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters.
HYPOTHESIS: DINO-affinity-refined pseudo-masks improve held-out PRO by at least 3 points over unrefined MIL maps, and the resulting segmentation branch retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: pseudo-mask refinement (none vs. DINO affinity propagation vs. CLIP-feature affinity). Stage 1: top-k MIL on the seg branch (image labels only). Stage 2: for each abnormal training image, compute DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features at 238x238 (17x17 patches, matching MVFA's grid), affinity A_ij = max(0, cos)^beta (beta = 8), row-normalise, propagate the stage-1 map m: m' = (alpha A + (1 - alpha) I)^t m with alpha = 0.7, t = 3; pseudo-mask = m' > 0.5 x max(m'). Stage 3: train seg adapters with Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask IoU against true masks (analysis only), pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Image-level MIL localises only the few most anomalous patches and produces fragmented maps. DINO features are spatially coherent and cluster anatomically consistent regions, so affinity propagation over DINO patch similarities can grow MIL seeds into region-shaped pseudo-masks, giving the segmentation branch dense, shape-aware supervision without any expert mask.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1 as top-k MIL on seg tokens (loss.py: topk_mil). 2) New script refine_masks.py: torch.hub DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (frozen, about 22M parameters), resize to 238, patch features 17x17x384, affinity and propagation in numpy; save pseudo-masks. 3) Stage 3: existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for all source images (normal: empty). 4) DINO is used only offline on source training images, not at test time, so inference cost is unchanged. 5) Hyper-parameters: alpha, beta, t as above (ablations alpha in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, t in {1, 3, 5}).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); masks of the source datasets are discarded for all image-label-supervised variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities using image AUROC only (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds; evaluation on the held-out modalities that have masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) for pixel metrics and on all six for image AUROC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only; CLIP-affinity propagation (same procedure with CLIP layer-24 features). Ablations: propagation parameters; DINOv2 ViT-S vs. ViT-B. Metrics: pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC; pseudo-mask IoU (analysis). Falsification: no PRO gain over MIL-only.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Two-stage anomaly-aware anchors then patch MIL, all from image labels
SUMMARY: Stage 1 learns residual text adapters that separate normal and abnormal anchors using image-level labels and an orthogonality term; stage 2 trains MVFA's segmentation adapters with top-k patch MIL against the frozen stage-1 anchors.
HYPOTHESIS: Anomaly-aware anchors learned from image labels increase held-out pixel AUROC of MIL-trained segmentation adapters by at least 2 points over frozen template anchors, and the combined method retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: anchor type during MIL (frozen template-average anchors vs. stage-1 anomaly-aware anchors). Stage 1: a residual MLP adapter on the text encoder output (ratio 0.1) trained for 10 epochs with image-level BCE on the CLS token similarity and an orthogonality penalty |cos(T_nor, T_abn)| (weight 0.1). Stage 2: seg adapters trained with top-k MIL (k = 6) and the all-patches-normal term for normal images, anchors frozen. Dependent variables: anchor separation (cosine), pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Under image-level supervision, MIL localisation depends entirely on how well the text anchors separate normal and abnormal patches; MVFA's anchors are frozen template averages. Following AA-CLIP, the anchors can first be made anomaly-aware using image labels only, and patch alignment by MIL then operates against a better-separated reference.
METHOD: 1) New module text_adapter.py: TextAdapter(d=768, bottleneck=192) applied residually to the two anchor embeddings. 2) train_anchor.py (stage 1): freeze CLIP and visual adapters; optimise TextAdapter with BCE(sigmoid(t * (cos(cls, T_abn) - cos(cls, T_nor))), y) + 0.1 |cos(T_nor, T_abn)| on all source images; lr 1e-4, 10 epochs. 3) train_zero.py (stage 2): replace seg_loss with topk_mil + normal-all-patches term against stage-1 anchors; det branch unchanged. 4) Test: test_zero.py with stage-1 anchors.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); masks of the source datasets are discarded for all image-label-supervised variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities using image AUROC only (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds; evaluation on the held-out modalities that have masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) for pixel metrics and on all six for image AUROC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL with frozen anchors; MIL with jointly (single-stage) learned anchors. Ablations: orthogonality weight; adapter bottleneck; stage-1 epochs. Metrics: anchor cosine, pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no gain over frozen anchors.
